faqs.question: Does Luna only cover planets?
faqs.answer: No. Luna's catalog is built for planets, moons, satellites, and other celestial bodies. The app can grow as the JSON catalog grows.

faqs.question: Does Luna require AR?
faqs.answer: No. AR mode is available on supported iPhone and iPad devices, but Luna also includes a full visual mode for exploring scenes without AR.

faqs.question: What NASA content does Luna use?
faqs.answer: Luna uses NASA/JPL textures, NASA Scientific Visualization Studio imagery, NASA 3D assets, and NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day. Source credits are included in the app.

faqs.question: Is Luna endorsed by NASA?
faqs.answer: No. Luna credits NASA sources where used, but Luna is an independent app and is not endorsed by NASA.

faqs.question: How is the body catalog loaded?
faqs.answer: The app uses a local JSON-backed catalog for body facts, orbit values, tags, texture names, model names, and related body data.

faqs.question: What is Astronomy Picture of the Day?
faqs.answer: NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day, often called APOD, is a daily image or video with title, date, explanation, and attribution. Luna includes APOD as part of its discovery experience.

faqs.question: Where can I download Luna?
faqs.answer: Luna is currently available through TestFlight. The download link on this site will be changed to the App Store link later.
